decisions.decision: What 'normal' release day would have been
decisions.chosen: log(count) = weekday level + linear trend, fitted on every counted day before the candidate; one-sided t on the prediction error
decisions.detail: user, 20 Nov: a formal hypothesis test that the drop is significant; the model was fixed before the result was computed: weekday levels for the weekly cycle, a trend for GitHub's growth, logs so changes are relative

decisions.chosen: the same test on every earlier day with >= 21 days of history
decisions.detail: an empirical check that does not lean on the t distribution: how often an ordinary day lands this far below its prediction

decisions.chosen: counted days up to release day with an earlier same-weekday day; the first week, later days and uncounted days are left out
decisions.detail: user, 20 Nov: test 19 Nov against what came before it; a day with nothing before it cannot be predicted, and a day after release is not a placebo

decisions.chosen: (placebo days at or below release day's t + 1) / (placebo days + 1)
decisions.detail: the standard rank p-value that counts release day itself, so it is never zero

decisions.chosen: release day's week-on-week change against the earlier same-weekday changes, prediction t with n - 1 df
decisions.detail: uses only the Thursdays, with no model of the trend

notes: applied without a refactor comparison, and static row attribution did not establish the results were kept: fct_github_day_surprise, fct_github_release_day_test; if the change was meant to keep them, that is unverified
